battle.name: 靖康之變
battle.theater: 汴京內外城與河北、山西前線
battle.brief: 靖康元年金軍三路南下，兩度圍困東京汴京，四十日與三十三日後外城內城相繼陷落，徽欽二帝連同宗室百官被押北去，北宋覆亡。卡面的十字弩並非宋軍實配：宋人守城所恃是神臂弓與床子弩這類機械弩，原理同源，卻把射速、破甲與城頭射位推到極限，仍擋不住女真人的雲梯、撞車與穴地。

kit.name: 十字弩
kit.history: 弩把射速交給了機械，代價是裝填慢。城牆上它比長弓可靠，野戰裡它比長弓脆弱。

countries: 靖康之變是北宋末年女真金國發動的滅國戰爭，自一一二五年十月金軍三路南下起，至一一二七年四月徽欽二帝被押離汴京止，前後約一年半。金是完顏氏女真於一一一五年建立的政權，太祖完顏阿骨打一一二三年病卒後由太宗完顏吳乞買即位，軍政大權分握於宗室將領之手。晉國公完顏宗望領西路大軍自燕京南下，完顏宗翰領中路大軍自雲中、太原方向南下，另遣別將經燕雲南口策應，兩路會師於汴京城下。金軍以女真猛安謀克為骨幹，配契丹、漢人、奚人降兵與被俘北人，騎兵居先，步兵繼之，另設打軍與攻具隊，專司架梯、掘地道、撞門與運糧。宋方是完整的北宋中央與地方軍政體系：樞密院掌兵籍與調發，三衙領殿前司、侍衛親軍司、步軍司三類禁軍，東京留守府統帥城防民兵與厢軍，各路節度使轄下的厢軍與鄉兵則是可被徵發的勤王兵。外圍還有遼的殘餘勢力：金陵舊臣南逃，契丹貴族西遷建立西遼；金占區後又扶植漢人傀儡劉豫建立偽齊；西夏全程觀望，未出兵。金攻宋的主要方向是河北與山西兩條平原地帶，汴京是唯一的目標，開封府、太原府、真定府、河間府、真定路一線的城邑屢攻屢下，最後全部指向東京。
countriesEn: The Jingkang Disaster was the war of extinction that the Jurchen Jin state launched against the Northern Song in the closing years of the twelfth century, running from the three-pronged invasion of October 1125 to the removal of the two emperors from Bianjing in the fourth month of 1127, a matter of roughly a year and a half. Jin was the polity the Wanyan clan of the Jurchens had founded in 1115; after the founder Wanyan Aguda died of illness in 1123 the throne passed to the Taizong, Wanyan Wuqimai, and military and political authority was held in the hands of the clan's generals. The Duke of Jin, Wanyan Zongwang, led the western column south from Yanjing, while Wanyan Zonghan led the central column down from Yunzhong and Taiyuan, with other commanders moving through the southern passes of Yan and Yun to support them; the two columns met under the walls of Bianjing. The Jin army had the Jurchen meng'an mouke as its backbone, filled out with Khitan, Han and Xi men from the surrendered and the enslaved, with cavalry in front and infantry behind, and with separate siege units assigned to raising ladders, driving mines, battering gates and hauling grain. The Song side was the whole of the Northern Song's central and local military-administrative system: the Privy Council held the rolls and the dispatch, the Three Commands administered the palace guards, the imperial guard and the infantry guard, the office of the capital governor of Dongjing commanded the city defence with its militia and its locally raised troops, and the locally raised troops and village levies of the circuit commanders were the men who could be summoned as a relief army. Around them stood the remains of the Liao: officials of the old southern capital fled south, the Khitan nobility migrated west to found the Western Liao, and in the occupied zone Jin set up the Han puppet Liu Yu as the Qi; Western Xia watched the whole war through without entering it. The main axes of the Jin advance were the open plains of Hebei and Shanxi, and Bianjing was the only objective: Kaifeng fu, Taiyuan fu, Zhending fu, Hejian fu and the line of Zhending lu were taken and retaken, and everything pointed at last towards the eastern capital.
people: 宋方最關鍵的人物是樞密使兼東京留守李綱。他在一二六年正月金軍逼近時接手城防，組織弓弩、撞竿、拒馬分層守備，派舟隊切斷汴河浮橋、斷金人糧道，並在夜裡火燒金軍攻城器具，撐過第一次圍城四十日。另一條線是宰相李邦彥與樞密使耿南仲一派主和，一二六年二月徽宗退位、欽宗即位，以割地賠款為條件，金軍才第一次退兵；樞密院的宦官童貫、梁師成與宰相王黼長期干政，軍備與財政一塌糊塗。守太原的知府張叔夜在西路戰線最烈處力戰殉城，樞密院右軍統制姚古、劉錫率勤王兵在汴京西北諸處屢戰屢敗，使第二度解圍的希望落空。民間方士郭京自稱能役六甲神兵，率數千妖兵守城，城破之日奉命突圍，全軍覆沒，一支號稱無堅不摧的軍隊在城門前自行瓦解。康王趙構事亂時正在外任副元帥，脫離汴京，後在南京應天府即位，是為宋高宗，此後三十年的南朝局面由他開端。金方則是完顏宗望與完顏宗翰兄弟：前者統西路攻燕京、圍汴京、扶二帝北遷，返程中病逝軍中；後者統中路破太原、進逼汴京，是金國中期權力最大的宗室，完顏宗弼日後清算他。完顏阿離骨等別將分統各路，金太宗完顏吳乞買在會寧坐鎮，遠程調度糧械。西夏的趙氏朝廷與南方的宋室、偽齊之間的三角，往來於金與宋的書信之中，這場戰爭的勝負，最後仍然落在兩個皇帝與兩位宗室大將的手上。
peopleEn: The decisive figure on the Song side was Li Gang, vice commissioner of the privy council and governor of the eastern capital. When the Jin army closed in in the first month of 1126 he took over the city defence, organised crossbows, pikes and cheval-de-frise into a layered defence, sent boat parties to cut the floating bridge on the Bian canal and sever the Jin supply line, and burned the Jin siege equipment at night, holding out through the forty days of the first siege. The other line was the chancellor Li Bangyan together with the vice commissioner Geng Nanzhong, who favoured peace: in the second month of 1126 the retired emperor handed the throne to his son and the Song offered territorial cessions and indemnities, and only then did the Jin withdraw for the first time. The eunuchs Tong Guan and Liang Shicheng of the privy council and the chancellor Wang Fu governed for long stretches, and the military and the finances were a ruin by the time the war came. Zhang Shuye, governor of Taiyuan, fought to the death on the fiercest stretch of the western front; the commanders Yao Gu and Liu Xi of the Right Army of the privy council led the relief troops into defeat again and again in the districts north-west of Bianjing, and the hope of a second relief dissolved with them. The popular charlatan Guo Jing claimed he could command the spirits of the six armour, led several thousand of his irregulars in the defence, and on the day the city fell was ordered to break out of the north gate with them, where the whole force was destroyed, a corps that had called itself invulnerable disintegrating at the gate itself. The Prince of Kang, Zhao Gou, was outside the capital as deputy commander when the trouble began and got clear of Bianjing; he was later enthroned at Yingtian fu in Nanjing as Song Gaozong, and the southern state of the next thirty years began with him. On the Jin side were the brothers Wanyan Zongwang and Wanyan Zonghan: the first commanded the western column, took Yanjing, besieged Bianjing and escorted the two emperors north, and died of illness on the return march; the second commanded the central column, broke Taiyuan and pressed down on Bianjing, and was the most powerful member of the clan in the middle years of Jin, only to be purged later by Wanyan Zongbi. Other commanders such as Wanyan Alibo led separate columns, while the Taizong Wanyan Wuqimai sat at Huining and handled the long-range flow of grain and equipment. The exchanges of letters between Jin, the Western Xia court of the Zhao and the Song court, and between Jin and the puppet Qi, ran alongside all of this, but the outcome of the war still came down to two emperors and two great generals of the clan.
kits: 卡面是十字弩：一具歐洲式的手持弩，弩臂、機關與踏板把拉力交給機械代勞，射程與破甲力都勝過長弓，代價是裝填緩慢，離開掩體便難以續射。它並非宋軍的制式裝備，但它指向的技術方向宋人走得比歐洲更遠：宋軍的機械化射擊以神臂弓、蹶張弓與床子弩為主。神臂弓弓長三尺五寸、矢長一尺八寸，靠臂力張弦，射得比長弓遠，且能穿重甲；床子弩有固定弩架與上下望山，一人即可操作，專供城頭與野外部署，是守城射擊的骨幹。守方還備有撞竿、拒馬、鐵蒺藜、竹篙與皮網，專對付雲梯；火器方面已有震天雷一類的爆炸物與火矢、火箭，用於燒毀攻城梯與封堵地道。弩手的編制在宋軍中是專職的弓弩手營，與長弓手分列城頭垛口。金軍的裝備體系正相反：重裝札甲的鐵浮圖騎兵結陣破陣，強弓與強弩百張齊射，遠探數百騎繞射牽制援軍，並攜帶大量牛羊隨軍就食，雲梯、撞車與穴地所用之具多屬臨時製造，攻城器械體量小、數量有限。攻守雙方最大的短板是同一個：攻城方缺乏成熟到足以對付三重城防的工程手段，守方缺乏能在城外野戰中扭轉局面的遠程衝擊力，於是四十日的僵持最後是靠外交而不是靠攻城技術收場。
kitsEn: The card shows a crossbow: a European hand bow whose stock, lock and stirrup hand the draw over to the machine, giving it greater range and better armour penetration than a longbow, at the cost of a slow reload that leaves it helpless once it leaves cover. It was not a standard piece of Song equipment, but the technical direction it points along was carried further by the Song than in Europe: the mechanical shooting of the Song army rested on the shenbi bow, the juzhang bow and the bed crossbow. The shenbi bow was three feet five inches in the bow and its bolt a foot eight inches, was drawn by arm strength, outranged the longbow and could pierce heavy armour; the bed crossbow had a fixed frame with an upper and lower sight, could be worked by a single man, and was issued for city walls and for field deployment, forming the backbone of the defending fire. The defenders also carried pikes, cheval-de-frise, iron caltrops, bamboo poles and hide nets, all of them meant for ladders, and among their weapons were explosive devices such as the thunder-shaking bomb together with fire arrows and rockets, used to burn siege ladders and seal mine tunnels. The crossbow crews in Song service were formed into specialist units, the bow and crossbow hands working their own section of the parapet, in line with the longbowmen. The Jin equipment system ran the other way: heavily armoured lancers of the iron-tower type fought in closed formation, strong bows and strong crossbows fired in files of a hundred, several hundred light horsemen rode round the flank to keep the relief army busy, and huge numbers of cattle and sheep travelled with the army for food, while the ladders, battering rams and mining tools were mostly made up on the spot, the siege train being small in bulk and short in numbers. The shortcoming was the same on both sides: the besiegers lacked engineering means mature enough to face a triple line of defences, and the defenders lacked any long-range shock that could turn the open field outside the walls, which is why forty days of stalemate ended in diplomacy rather than in a breakthrough.
tactics: 金軍的戰術骨架是分進合擊加上打援。一一二五年十月三路南下，中路與西路以騎兵快速切斷河北、山西方向的勤王援軍，在汴京以西的白溝河、開封、復州、頤州一線以傾斜兵力的騎戰反覆衝散宋軍，迫各路援軍不敢近城，第一次圍城就這樣靠「不救城」取勝。城下的攻法有兩種：一是疊盾結陣抵近牆根，雲梯十數架同時靠城，梯頂以長刀砍擊垛口，壕溝被屍體與土石填平，填土兵直衝門；二是穴地掘道攻門，並以撞車撞擊城門、以火藥焚燒門板。第一次圍城攻了約四十日不下，金人自己也承認不習於攻宋之堅城，遂以割地賠款為條件退兵；第二次南下改以掃清沿途援軍為先，目標是攻下汴京、擄走二帝。守城方在李綱手上有一套可行的辦法：城頭分列弓弩、槊刀與撞竿，前排以撞竿頂住雲梯，後排以神臂弓覆射城下密集之敵，夜間派小隊出城焚燒攻城器具，遣水軍拆斷汴河浮橋斷其糧道，又以敢死之士貼城搶修被毀的垛口。問題出在體制：勤王兵號稱四十餘萬，卻分屬數十路節度使，無統一指揮，糧餉不濟，援軍到了汴京外仍各自求戰，屢為金騎擊破，第二次圍城時的解圍遂成一廢話。城破之後，欽宗赴軍營請罪，金人索繳金銀輜重，押二帝北行，這場戰役在戰術層面其實以宋廷放棄野戰、把一切押在城牆與外交上的選擇開始，也以金人繞開宋人擅長的城防、專打援軍與糧道的打法結束。
tacticsEn: The skeleton of the Jin method was a converging advance combined with an attack on the relief. In October 1125 the three columns came south, the central and western ones using cavalry to cut the relief armies in Hebei and Shanxi, and on the line of the Baigou river, Kaifeng, Fuzhou and Yizhou west of Bianjing they broke Song detachments again and again with cavalry outnumbering them locally, so that no relief army dared approach the city; the first siege was won precisely by this refusal to relieve the city. There were two ways of taking the walls. One was to close up with overlapping shields, bring up a dozen or more ladders at once, and cut at the parapet from the top with long blades while the ditch outside was filled with bodies and rubble, the soldiers who followed simply running at the gate over the fill. The other was to drive a mine under the gate and batter it with a ram, burning the door with powder. The first siege failed after about forty days, the Jin themselves conceding that they were unused at storming a Song city of this strength, and they withdrew on condition of territorial cessions and indemnities. The second invasion swept the relief armies off the roads first, and the object was Bianjing itself and the two emperors. The defence under Li Gang had methods that worked: on the walls the crossbows, long lances and pikes were posted in tiers, the front rank bracing the ladders with pikes and the rear rank sweeping the crowded enemy below with shenbi bows, small parties went out at night to burn the siege equipment, boat crews broke the floating bridge on the Bian canal to cut the grain road, and volunteers worked at the wall in the open to repair parapets shot away. The problem was institutional. The relief host was numbered at more than four hundred thousand, but it belonged to dozens of circuit commanders, had no unified command and no supply; the relief armies reached the outskirts of Bianjing and each sought battle on its own account, only to be beaten by the Jin horse again and again, so that the second siege ended with the question of relief turning into empty talk. After the fall, the Qinzong emperor came to the camp to surrender, the Jin demanded the gold, silver and baggage, and the two emperors were marched north. At the tactical level this campaign began with the Song court's decision to abandon the open field and stake everything on the walls and on diplomacy, and it ended with the Jin method of avoiding what the Song were good at and striking instead at the relief armies and the supply line.
data: 可核對的數字集中在人數、圍城日數與俘獲三處。金軍第一次入宋的總兵力，《宋史》記為十五萬，分三道；第二次南下兵額增至二十萬上下，其中西路十五萬、東路五萬，圍汴京的實戰兵力仍以萬計。防守一方能核的數字是勤王兵四十餘萬，以及北宋禁軍名額接近百萬而實數遠低於此；四十萬對二十萬的對比說明宋廷不是無人，而是無統一指揮、無糧餉、士氣不齊。圍城時間：第一次自靖康元年正月二十日前後金軍逼城至二月退兵，前後約四十日；第二次自靖康元年十一月圍城至十二月末汴京城破，約三十三日。城防尺度見於《宋史·地理志》：東京外城周約二十五里，內城周約十一里，外城之外有護龍河，闊數十步，橋上皆有營壘。物資方面，金軍出師時攜牛羊數十萬頭，河北、山西州縣的糧食被就地徵發；宋廷靠汴河漕運維持城內所需，並在圍城期間括取民間米糧，軍器、弓弦與箭的儲備經四十日消耗後所剩有限。俘獲方面，《靖康稗史》等所記被押北行者包含徽宗、欽宗、諸王、后妃、宗室、百官、侍從與工匠，車駕逾千輛，人數以數十萬計；同一批記錄還列出被帶走的內府圖籍、禮器、樂器、織造與軍器。這些數字來自事後追述，具體名目多有重複與誇張，可當作量級而非精確統計。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked cluster in three places: numbers of men, numbers of days, and numbers of captives. The total strength with which Jin entered Song territory the first time is given in the History of Song as one hundred and fifty thousand, divided into three columns; on the second descent the total rose to something like two hundred thousand, of which the western column was a hundred and fifty thousand and the eastern five, though the force actually investing Bianjing was still counted in the tens of thousands. On the defending side the figures that can be checked are the relief host of more than four hundred thousand and the near-million establishment of the Song imperial guards, the actual strength being far below paper; the contrast of four hundred thousand against two hundred thousand shows that the Song court was not short of men but short of unified command, of supply and of the will to fight. Duration: the first siege, from the Jin approach to the city around the twentieth day of the first month of Jingkang to the withdrawal in the second month, lasted about forty days; the second, from the investment in the eleventh month of Jingkang to the fall of Bianjing at the end of the twelfth month, about thirty-three days. The scale of the defences is recorded in the Geography section of the History of Song: the outer wall of the eastern capital ran about twenty-five li, the inner wall about eleven li, and outside the outer wall ran a defensive moat, several tens of paces wide, with camp works on every bridge across it. On stores: the Jin army went out with several hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep and took grain from the prefectures and counties of Hebei and Shanxi as it advanced; the Song court kept the city supplied by the Bian canal and requisitioned grain from the population during the siege, and the stock of arms, bowstrings and arrows left after forty days of expenditure was thin. On the captives: the Jingkang Baoshi and similar records list those marched north as including the retired emperor and the reigning emperor, the princes, the empresses and consorts, the clan, the officials, the attendants and the craftsmen, with over a thousand vehicles of the imperial train and a number of people in the tens of thousands; the same records itemise the palace library, the ritual vessels, the musical instruments, the weaving works and the military stores carried off. These numbers come from accounts written after the fact, with much duplication and exaggeration in the itemised lists, and they should be read as orders of magnitude rather than as exact returns.
cause: 打起來的原因是三層疊加。最外層是海上之盟的後果：北宋聯金滅遼，金得燕雲十六州，遼亡而宋不取地，反而自斷屏障，讓金國在北方無所牽制，可以把兵鋒直指中原；盟約中承諾給宋的歲幣與燕雲歸宋之事，金人此後一概不認。中層是金廷的戰略轉向：完顏阿骨打建國與滅遼時，本以邊部反擊為主，去世後完顏吳乞買接位，改採攻勢，認定宋廷軍弱財廣，據河北、山西之地，攻取汴京可取全局，遂於一一二五年十月分三路南侵。最內層是北宋自身的崩解：蔡京把持朝政二十年，斂財括民，軍費不足，禁軍雖多而空額極多、久未操演；弓弩與城防器械缺乏合格工匠與儲備，和平久了無人知兵；宦官童貫、梁師成以樞密院之權干政，宰相王黼、蔡攸之輩只知揣摩上意；朝中主戰與主和兩派相持，處置一拖再拖。於是第一次圍城時，一二六年二月徽宗退位、欽宗即位，以割太原、中山、河間等州並輸大量金銀絹帛為條件，金軍才退兵。這個羞辱性的妥協反而證實宋廷軟弱，第二次南侵便不再談判，直取汴京。
causeEn: The causes were three layers deep. The outermost was the consequence of the alliance made at sea: the Northern Song had joined with Jin to destroy the Liao, Jin took the sixteen prefectures of Yan and Yun, the Liao perished, and the Song did not take the land, cutting away their own screen instead, so that Jin was left with nothing to hold it in the north and could turn its arms straight towards the central plain; the annual payments and the return of Yan and Yun promised to the Song under the terms of that alliance were henceforth denied by Jin in every particular. The middle layer was the strategic turn of the Jin court: while Wanyan Aguda was alive, the state had fought defensively along the frontier, but after his death the Taizong Wanyan Wuqimai took the offensive, judged the Song weak in war and rich in treasure, and reasoned that from Hebei and Shanxi a blow at Bianjing would carry the whole game; hence the three columns sent south in October 1125. The innermost layer was the collapse of the Northern Song itself: Cai Jing had held the government for twenty years, squeezing wealth out of the people, so that military funds were short; the imperial guards were numerous on paper but heavily short of their rolls and long untrained; arms, crossbows and siege equipment lacked skilled craftsmen and adequate stores, and a long peace had left nobody who knew the business of war; the eunuchs Tong Guan and Liang Shicheng used their authority in the privy council to interfere in affairs of state, and chancellors of the type of Wang Fu and Cai You did nothing but gauge the emperor's mood; the parties for war and for peace deadlocked, and every decision was deferred. Hence at the first siege, in the second month of 1126 the retired emperor gave up the throne to his son, and the Song offered the cession of Taiyuan, Zhongshan, Hejian and other prefectures together with large payments in gold, silver and silk, and only then did the Jin army withdraw. That humiliating compromise instead proved that the court was soft, and the second invasion of 1126 ceased to be a negotiation and became a direct march on Bianjing.
impact: 北宋覆亡的後果遠大於一場戰役的勝負。政治上，宋室南渡，在南京應天府即位後遷都臨安，中原的官僚、軍人與手工藝者大批南遷，衣冠南渡成為此後百年的最大人口移動，南方州縣的稅收與人口比重因此反超北方，宋也從一個統一帝國變成一偏安朝堂。經濟上，重心南移完成，泉州、廣州、明州的海舶貿易在失去北方陸路之後暴增，絲綢、茶與瓷器的外銷及南洋與日本市場的開拓，改變了此後數百年的東亞貿易格局；金與西夏的絲路貿易則在西北一線收縮。對北方而言，金取得中原後以漢式衙門與州縣治理，先設燕京樞密院、汴京留守司，猛安謀克軍戶大批移居漢地，與漢人爭田、爭役，激出河北與湖湘的漢軍叛金與起義，劉豫的偽齊正是在這股矛盾中被扶植起來的傀儡；金廷宗室與后宮的權力鬥爭也由此加劇，完顏宗翰一代的權勢最終內耗於自相殘殺。文化上，內府圖書、禮器與工藝被大批北運，中原文物斷層，靖康二字自此成為士人筆下的傷心詞；對南方的人而言，它又成了一面旗，岳飛等北伐將領以此為號召，兩宋三百年的正統之爭就此拉開。
impactEn: The consequences of the fall of the Northern Song reached far beyond the result of a single campaign. Politically the Song house moved south, was enthroned at Yingtian fu in Nanjing and later moved its capital to Lin'an; officials, soldiers and craftsmen of the central plain migrated south in great numbers, the migration of the scholar-official class becoming the largest population movement of the following century, and the revenue and population of the southern prefectures came to outweigh the north, so that the Song changed from a unified empire into a court living on one corner of its former territory. Economically the shift of the centre of gravity was completed: maritime trade out of Quanzhou, Guangzhou and Mingzhou grew rapidly once the northern land routes were lost, and the export of silk, tea and porcelain and the opening of the markets of the southern seas and of Japan changed the East Asian trading pattern for centuries afterwards, while the silk-road trade of Jin and Western Xia contracted on the north-western axis. For the north, having taken the central plain Jin governed it with Chinese-style offices and prefectures, first establishing the Yanking privy council and the Bianjing resident office, and it moved large numbers of meng'an mouke military households into Han lands, where they competed with Han farmers for land and for corvée, and this provoked the Han troops' rebellions against Jin in Hebei and in Hunan; the puppet Qi of Liu Yu was raised precisely out of that contradiction. And the struggle for power between the clan and the court at the Jin court grew out of it as well, the power of the Zonghan generation in the end consumed by internal purges. On the cultural side the palace library, the ritual vessels and the workshops were carried north in bulk, the cultural record of the central plain was broken, and from that day the two characters of Jingkang became a word for heartbreak in the writing of the scholars; to the people of the south it became a banner, and generals such as Yue Fei raised their appeal under it, and the three-hundred-year argument of the two Song houses over the legitimate succession was opened from that point.
result: 結果是北宋在戰爭中滅亡，而南宋在南方重建。靖康二年四月，金人把徽宗、欽宗及后妃、諸王、宗室、百官、侍從與工匠編入隊伍，用車駕押送出汴京，經河北、燕山北去；徽宗途中病重，次年五月死於北方，欽宗亦於一一三五年間死於金國地界。康王趙構於同年五月在南京應天府即位，是為高宗，軍政大權先後在張浚、呂頤浩等主戰與主和諸人之手轉移，此後經黃天蕩、撫州、房州一連串敗績，遷都杭州，以臨安為行在。此後的戰局是另一段長跑：一四〇年岳飛在郾城、柘皋一線擊敗金軍，逼近黃河；一一四一年底至一一四二年初的紹興和議與澠淵之盟，割唐、鄧二州，向金稱臣，歲貢銀絹各二十五萬，換來百餘年的邊界相安，金與南朝自此在淮水至大散關一線對峙。對金而言，它贏了戰役卻沒有贏下戰爭：南方未能北還，北方秩序在四十年間被軍戶矛盾與南下的蒙古逐步掏空，最終金亡於蒙古人之手；北宋丟掉的北方土地沒有回到中原，而南宋也終於一二七九年崖山之役。
resultEn: The result was that the Northern Song perished in the war and the Southern Song was rebuilt in the south. In the fourth month of Jingkang two the Jin took the retired emperor, the reigning emperor, the empresses and consorts, the princes, the clan, the officials, the attendants and the craftsmen, formed them up in columns, and marched them out of Bianjing in the imperial wagons by way of Hebei and the Yanshan mountains; the retired emperor fell ill on the road and died in the north the following May, and the reigning emperor also died on Jin soil around 1135. The Prince of Kang, Zhao Gou, was enthroned at Yingtian fu in Nanjing in the same month of May and became Gaozong; command of the war passed in turn among Zhang Jun, Lü Yihao and the men of both the war and peace factions, and after a run of defeats at Huangtiandang, Fuzhou and Fangzhou the court moved its capital to Hangzhou and made Lin'an the seat of government. What followed was a different, longer contest: in 1140 Yue Fei beat the Jin at Yancheng and Zhegao and drove them up to the Yellow River; the Shaoxing settlement and the treaty of Chanyuan in the last months of 1141 and the opening months of 1142 ceded Tang and Deng, acknowledged Jin as overlord and paid tribute of 250,000 taels of silver and bolts of silk a year, and bought more than a century of quiet on the border, Jin and the southern court facing each other from the Huai to the Dasong Pass. For Jin it won the campaign and not the war: the south was never recovered, and the order of the north was hollowed out over forty years by the quarrel between military households and settlers and by the Mongols pressing down from the north, until Jin fell to the Mongols; the northern lands the Northern Song had lost did not come back to the central plain, and the Southern Song in turn ended at the battle of Yamen in 1279.
